title: Runtime probe adapter for blockwise kernel selection
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Problem: The current kernel selector uses coarse heuristics that mispredict optimal kernels for workloads with bimodal sequence length distributions and mixed attention tiling. This causes suboptimal throughput or unexpected latency spikes for certain tenants when their traffic mixes long prefill requests with short decode bursts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime 'microprobe' adapter that performs short, per-node microbenchmarks and maintains a small per-GPU blockwise fingerprint table (by architecture+seqlen-range+batch) to drive kernel choices for both prefill and decode paths. The adapter should be budgeted (probe budget), low-overhead, and integrate with the existing kernel routing policy and prefill/decode scheduler so choices remain stable across a single request's lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Microprobe runs in <2% runtime overhead on steady-state throughput for 99% of traffic
Observed kernel selection accuracy improves p95 token latency by >=6% on mixed seqlen benchmarks
Per-GPU fingerprint table persisted across restarts and exposed in Console metrics
Fallback to default heuristic if probe budget exhausted or probe fails
End-to-end tests covering prefill->decode kernel invariants and KV cache compatibility
implementation_notes: Design microprobe as an asynchronous sampler that runs short forward-only passes (configurable tokens 16/32/64) against candidate kernels on a warmed allocator
Fingerprint key composed of {gpu_arch, memory_tier, seqlen_bucket, batch_size, attention_tile} hashed to small table (64-256 entries) per device
Probe budget: default 1 probe per 1k requests for new fingerprint, LRU eviction policy for table entries

Signal integration: adapter emits a kernel_hint token in the request context; scheduler must ensure prefill and subsequent decode choose compatible kernel variants (same KV layout) or trigger safe fallback
Metrics: probe_latency, probe_success_rate, hint_adoption_rate, hint_regression_alerts (compare with baseline kernels)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: probes could evict useful allocations or cause transient OOM on constrained nodes. Mitigation: run probes on separate probe stream with soft memory cap and use allocator snapshots to rollback allocations.
Risk: inconsistent kernel across prefill/decode may corrupt KV cache. Mitigation: require kernel compatibility tag; if incompatible, do not change kernel mid-request and mark hint as mismatched.
Risk: noisy probes may oscillate choices. Mitigation: add exponential backoff for fingerprint churn and hysteresis window before switching production kernel.
milestones: 2025-02-20: RFC + design review with Serving and Runtime teams
2025-02-28: Prototype microprobe lib and in-memory fingerprint table
2025-03-07: Integrate kernel_hint into router and scheduler; add Console instrumentation
2025-03-14: Run cluster canary on dev pool with mixed seqlen synthetic traffic

testing_plan: Unit: microprobe correctness against mocked kernels and failing probe scenarios
Perf: synthetic mixed-seqlen workload (70% short decode, 30% long prefill) against baseline heuristics
Stability: long-running soak with probe budget set to 5% of traffic and verification of allocator rollback
Regression: KV-cache compatibility tests and end-to-end decode correctness checks
